name: Promptfoo
use_label: Test what your AI app actually answers
one_liner: Test and compare what your prompts, agents and RAG apps actually answer.

text.why: Every prompt change ends up judged by feel. Promptfoo runs the same inputs across models and prompt variants and lays the answers side by side in a matrix, with red-teaming for vulnerabilities in the same tool.
text.take: It replaces "that feels better" with a table you can point at. The repository states plainly that it joined OpenAI and stays open source under MIT.
build: A CLI and a library: install with npm, brew or pip, or run it with npx and install nothing. Provider keys go in as environment variables, results open as a browser matrix, and it drops into CI as a regression check.

who.role: People shipping AI features, and teams that must keep quality steady while the prompts keep changing.

start.text: Create an example with npx, run the eval and open the results view.

caveat: Needs Node.js 22.22 or newer. Calls run on your own provider keys, so a large eval costs real money there, and there is a paid enterprise edition alongside.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: A Promptfoo evaluation matrix: prompts and models across the top, test inputs down the side, each cell holding an answer and its pass mark.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
